description:
FILED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20) by #1501 round 11 (CHECK 2 on t/op/sprintf.t).

Four small, independent conversion facts; one task because they are one
formatter and none is worth a task alone.  Every line MEASURED vs perl 5.40.3
through the file's own data table (the row's description IS the expected text).

  1. NEGATIVE ZERO.  `sprintf "%.0g", -0.0` is `-0` in perl and `0` here.
     (op/sprintf.t 235; the row's own note says C99 mandates the sign.)
  2. `#` ON `%g`.  `sprintf "%#.0g", 12345.6789` is `1.e+04` in perl (the
     flag KEEPS the decimal point) and `1e+04` here.  (row 237)
  3. `%#p`.  perl renders a hex pointer matching `^0x[0-9a-f]+\s*$`; PCL's
     answer does not match.  (row 341)
  4. EXPLICIT INDEX WITH `*`.  `%*2$d` must consume the indexed argument and
     then report a missing one (`123 MISSING`); PCL prints `123`.
     `%3$*4$v*2$.*1$x` must format four reordered arguments; PCL rejects the
     whole directive as invalid.  `%*1073741819$v2d` must be rejected, and
     PCL rejects a DIFFERENT text.  (rows 553, 550, 540)

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/sprintf.t 235 237 341 540 550 553.

Sibling tasks that own the rest of this file: #1961 (the `%v` family), #1874
(`%n`), #1875 (an invalid conversion is copied literally), #1963 (`%a`).
subject: sprintf numeric-format residue: negative zero loses its sign, `%#` does not keep the decimal point, `%#p`, and the explicit-index `%N$` + `*` combinations (6 rows of t/op/sprintf.t)
